intro_bn: এই গাইড CBLM 9-কে পাতার ক্রম অনুযায়ী পড়ায়: আগে LO ও PC, তারপর তিনটি Information Sheet, প্রতিটির পরে তার Job/Activity/Specification Sheet, শেষে Review of Competency।

fields: Unit Code and Title: TVTENV502- Address learning needs and foster and promote a healthy, safe and inclusive learning culture

Unit Descriptor: This unit specifies the competency required to address learners' physiological, social and educational needs and foster and promote a safe learning environment which supports inclusive work practices and learning culture
blocks.note_bn: উপরে code ও title, nominal hours, descriptor; নিচে বামে element, ডানে তার performance criteria। চারটি element, মোট ১৬টি PC।
rows: 1. Develop technical and vocational learning programs and assessment methodology to take account of learner's language, literacy and numeracy skill levels and those required for the given level of training
1.1 Identify and document both individual and group OSH needs of the learners
1.2 Identify and document the level of language, literacy and numeracy skills required in the workplace using validated instruments and other sources of information.
1.3 Document and identified language, literacy and numeracy skills requirements for planning and implementing suitable learning program and assessment methods.
1.4 Customise Technical and Vocational learning programs taking account of individual learner's language, literacy or numeracy skills required for the level of training.
1.5 Select, customise or develop learning materials that are appropriate for the language, literacy or numeracy skills of learners.
2. Identify OSH issues and hazards in the learning environment
2.1 Research and access sources of information to identify OSH issues and hazards common within the industry in which the learning and/or assessment will take place
2.2 Inspect the learning environment prior to use to identify OSH issues and hazards that may be created by trainees
3. Assess risks in the learning environment and adopt appropriate measures

3.1 Assess the likelihood of injury as a result of exposure to identified hazard/s and prioritize for action based on severity of any potential injury, illness or negative/adverse outcome that may arise.
3.2 Implement and monitor supervisory arrangements appropriate to and/or trainees' levels of knowledge/skill/ experience to ensure their health and safety.
3.3 Provide trainees with appropriate information related to OSH and the use of protective gear (where applicable).
3.4 Assess trainees for knowledge of OSH requirements and the use of protective gears (where applicable).
3.5 Personal limitations in assessing OSH risks and implementing actions are recognised and specialist advisers are consulted when appropriate
3.6 Monitor and update OSH measures and procedures on a regular basis
4. Develop and implement work and learning strategies to support diversity and inclusivity
4.1 Establish the ground rules for participation and behaviour with colleagues, learners and clients through a cooperative, agreed process.
4.2 Identify, acknowledge and cater for individual differences as well as generic and particular needs of trainees in line with stated/documented national and organizational policies.
4.3 Model inclusiveness in the learning environment and personal work performance.

selfChecks.q_bn: আপনার trainee-র current competencies কীভাবে চিহ্নিত করবেন?
selfChecks.question: cblm09-sc1-q1

real.answer:
Trainees' current competency can be determined by pre-assessment.
The following are suggested methods you can use to pre-assess a trainee's
competencies.
1. Checking with the learner.
When you meet the trainee (first time), you can ask the learner to respond or
undergo a self-assessment instrument or subject them to an oral interview or
written test.
2. Analyse any pre-session information available, like enrolment form or -pre-
application form and other related documents such as;
•
Reports of previous competency assessment undertaken.
•
Resume or Curriculum Vitae.
•
Enterprise training and assessment records.
•
Performance Reports from Supervisor.
Answer 2
Trainee's training requirements or training needs can be determined by identifying
the gap between the required competencies as defined by the unit of competency
and the trainee's current competency.
The gap between the required competencies and the current competencies is the
portion of the skills and knowledge the learner needs to achieve to be recognized as
competent in a particular job.
Answer 3
The learner training requirements can be validated with the following
persons/officers.
•
Trainers, Teachers and Assessors.
•
Supervisors/ or trainees employers.
•
Participant Trainee/Learner who is advanced in skill.
•
Experts in the Trainees Trade Areas.
•
Government Regulatory bodies.
•
Consultative Committees.
•
Training Providers, employers and human resources departments.
•
Assessors/Assessment Centers.
Answer 4
A competency standard includes:
•
skills, knowledge and attitude requirements for the level of work
•
quality indicators
•
national qualifications that a person can receive who has been assessed as
competent against the national standards
•
learning strategies that provide guidance about the organisation of training,
including implementation guidelines and training/learning materials
•
assessment guidelines
•
assessment methods and materials
Answer 5
As mentioned above, a competency standard provides information about the
competencies associated with different occupations within a particular industry. They
ideally lead to national qualifications and include assessment guidelines.
A curriculum document serves as an implementation guide for a unit of competency
or course or module of study. For a curriculum document to be accepted by the
industries, it must be 'mapped' against the competencies in competency standards.
At this stage though, there are still many industries that do not have industry
competency standards developed.
Basically, competency standards establish the skills, knowledge and attitude required
for a particular industry. A curriculum interprets the competency standards so that it
can be delivered as a course in TVET institutions.

selfChecks.modelAnswer:
Three training methods:
1. Presentation: present information to small or large groups, with visual aids.
2. Demonstration: show learners a task or skill step by step, then practice.
3. Role-play: simulate real work; debriefing is essential.
Coaching vs mentoring:
- Coaching enables learning and development so performance improves. It is task oriented and performance driven.
- Mentoring is a developmental partnership where one person shares knowledge, skills, information and perspective. It is relationship oriented and development driven.
selfChecks.q_bn: তিনটি training method-এর নাম লিখুন। Coaching আর mentoring-এর পার্থক্য কী?
selfChecks.question: cblm09-sc2-q2

real.answer:
•
Presentation/discussion - most common and popular method of training
usually delivered as a speech by the teacher or instructor before the class or
students as a method of instruction
•
Demonstration - a display given to students by the teacher on how something
is done or how something works
•
Role Play - acting out of part: the acting out of a part, especially that of
somebody with a particular social role, in order to understand the role or
person better This process is used in psychotherapy and in training people in
interpersonal skills.
Difference between coaching and mentoring
Coaching is a process that enables learning and development to occur and thus
performance to improve. Coaching is task oriented and it is performance driven.
Mentoring is the developmental partnership through which one person shares
knowledge, skills, information and perspective to foster the personal and professional
growth of someone else. Mentoring is relationship oriented and development driven.

selfChecks.modelAnswer:
Links meet two key learning principles:
1. Learners remember best the first and last points of a learning session.
2. Learners need to tie new information into existing knowledge.
How: in the introduction, summarise the key points of the previous session and tie them in to the current session. In the review, refer to how this session relates to the next. For completely new material, relate it to life experience or a comparison.
selfChecks.q_bn: Learning session-গুলোর মধ্যে link কেন দিতে হয়?
selfChecks.question: cblm09-sc2-q4

real.answer:
Links are an important part of every-day life. When you learn something new, you will
normally relate it to something you already know. For example, if you were to buy a
new television, it is quite possible that the control switches would be in a different
place. Despite this, you would link in to your existing knowledge of televisions and
know what control switches to look for and some likely places for them to be situated.
Providing links between learning sessions meets two of the key learning principles
identified earlier: that learners remember best the first and last points of a learning
session, and that learners need to tie new information into existing knowledge.
Normally, the session that you are delivering will overlap or at least have some
relevance to the previous and next session. Where this is the case, you should, in
your introduction, summarise the key points from the previous session and tie them
in to the information to be covered in the current session. In your review, you should
refer to how this session will relate to the next.
If you are introducing completely new material, you should try to relate the
information to something that the learners will already know, either through life
experience or by use of an appropriate comparison.

selfChecks.modelAnswer:
Existing resources cannot simply be copied and distributed. Check:
1. Language: appropriate for the learners and level; jargon explained.
2. Relevance: to units of competency and their elements, and session learning outcomes.
3. Learner characteristics: safe and accessible, reflect diversity, no disrespect, learners can relate.
4. Checklist for selecting resources: e.g. current and accurate, gender sensitive, copyright considered.
5. Consumable resources: e.g. markers, printer paper, flip charts.

real.answer:
Depending upon what you are teaching/training, there may be a great deal of
resources that have already been developed that you can use in the learning
session, rather than developing your own.
However, the fact that they exist and may even have been developed specifically for
teaching does not mean that you can simply copy them and distribute them to the
learners.
There are several factors that need to be addressed in this regards;
•
Language
•
Relevance
•
Learner characteristics

Consumable resources

selfChecks.modelAnswer:
Things to consider while selecting a training venue:
1. The Right Fit: suits the type of event and impression.
2. Location: easy to get to; transport and car parking.
3. Cost: a fixed price including what you need.
4. The Facilities: meeting room, sound system, disabled access.
5. Your Objectives: be clear at the start.
6. Make a Site Visit.
7. Fit for Purpose: right room size and set up.
8. Building a Good Relationship with the venue staff.
